title: Post-outage verification and self-serve reconciliation guide
content:
Summary (customer-facing):

On 2026-08-25 at ~14:10 UTC we observed a regional inference degradation impacting a subset of customer requests routed to the eu-west-1 cluster. A portion of requests experienced delayed or out-of-order streaming responses. We triaged and implemented a staged mitigation by 15:05 UTC and full routing normalization by 16:40 UTC. All affected requests have been captured in an evidence bundle and are available for customer verification and optional replay.

Purpose of this doc: plain-language verification steps for customers, a compact timeline, choices customers can make (opt-in replay / accept non-replay reconciliation), and what evidence we provide to independently validate integrity. This is intended for technical owners and integration contacts.

What happened (plain language):
- Root cause (summary): a race between our KV/prefix cache eviction and an autoscale-driven worker replacement caused short-lived mismatches between request routing and in-memory KV caches. This led to some in-flight streaming sessions seeing partial cache misses and reordering of partial chunks.
- Impact: ~0.9% of streaming sessions in eu-west-1 during the 14:05–15:05 UTC window returned truncated or misordered chunks; non-streaming generation and embedding endpoints were largely unaffected.
- Scope: customers with streaming-enabled sessions or long-context generation that pinned to affected model variants.

Immediate mitigations performed:
1) Temporarily pinned routing to healthy pool (14:20 UTC) and disabled scale-down windows for the cluster (14:28 UTC).
2) Applied a cache eviction gate to avoid concurrent eviction during node handover (14:45 UTC).
3) Gradual rollback of risky kernel selection introduced in prior rollout (15:05 UTC).
4) Full traffic normalization verified by synthetic health checks (16:40 UTC).

Customer choices and recommended actions (pick one):
A) Opt-in replay (recommended if you see evidence of truncated or misordered outputs that affect downstream correctness). We will re-run affected requests with the same model+config and deliver outputs and a replay report. Replay is read-only and will not re-emit to end users unless you choose to reapply results.
B) Self-serve reconciliation (fast, no-replay): we provide a verification bundle and short heuristics you can run to confirm integrity; if you accept, no further action is needed.
C) Request SLA credit + manual forensic assistance: if you require adjudication beyond our automated evidence, choose assisted reconciliation and we will assign a solutions engineer.

What we provide in the evidence bundle (automated, per-tenant):
- Per-request metadata: request_id, tenant_id hash (one-way), timestamp, routed-node id, model-version tag, token counts.
- Streaming chunk checksums (SHA256 hex) and sequence indexes for each session.
- Operator timeline: precise ops actions with UTC times (e.g., gating, rollback markers).
- Synthetic test traces and health-check deltas that show before/after behavior.
- Replay inputs (exact prompt + model/config snapshot) and a replay sandbox ID you can use to run locally in our dedicated replay environment.

How to perform self-serve verification (steps for engineers):
1) Download your tenant bundle from the link below (signed URL, expiry 7 days).
2) For streaming sessions: verify per-chunk sequence indexes are strictly increasing and match checksums in order. If any chunk index is missing or checksum mismatch occurs, flag for replay.
3) For generation sessions: compare original output token count and final output checksum to replay outputs provided in the bundle.
4) If you elect no-replay: sign the short acknowledgement template (we provide) and notify cs@redwood.ai; we will close the customer-facing incident record.

Replay process (if you opt in):
- Replay window: replays will be scheduled during a 48-hour window after opt-in to avoid interfering with peak throughput.
- Replay semantics: we replay with identical model+quantization+config in an isolated sandbox that mirrors the runtime at the incident time.
- Deliverables: replay outputs, a delta report (where outputs differ), and a confidence score for each affected request.
- Retention: replay artifacts retained for 30 days by default; customers can request export.

SLA and credits:
- We will evaluate SLA impact per the committed SLO for your plan. If your account qualifies and the incident meets credit thresholds, we will apply a prorated usage credit. If you choose replay and the replay shows degraded outputs vs. baseline, credit application is expedited.

Timeline (concise):
- 2026-08-25 14:05 UTC: anomaly detected by synthetic checks
- 2026-08-25 14:10 UTC: first customer ticket arrives reporting truncated stream
- 2026-08-25 14:20 UTC: routing pinned to healthy pool
- 2026-08-25 14:28 UTC: scale-down disabled for cluster
- 2026-08-25 14:45 UTC: cache eviction gate enabled
- 2026-08-25 15:05 UTC: risky kernel rollout rollback initiated
- 2026-08-25 16:40 UTC: traffic normalized and synthetic health green

Technical appendix (short):
- Root cause detail: a new kernel-selection path that improved tail-latency inadvertently introduced a short window where worker handover occurred while eviction messages were inflight. Two concurrent events: (1) worker replacement triggered eviction of prefix-KV entries, (2) a small subset of requests were momentarily forwarded to a worker that had not yet warmed its KV layer, producing partial state reads.
- Permanent fixes planned: 1) strict handover fencing in the runtime to ensure eviction and handover are ordered; 2) safer rollout checks for kernel selection with a 0.5% traffic canary and stronger preflight; 3) enhanced per-session chunk IDs to detect reordering at ingestion.

Next steps for customers and how to opt in:
1) If you want us to prepare your evidence bundle and replay estimate, reply to this message with the single line: "OPT-IN-REPLAY <tenant-id>" to cs@redwood.ai.
2) If you prefer self-serve verification, reply with: "SELF-VERIFY <tenant-id>" and we will post the signed download link and the short acknowledgement template.
3) For assisted reconciliation or SLA adjudication, reply: "ASSIST <tenant-id>" — a solutions engineer will reach out within one business day.

Contact and escalation:
- Primary contact: Priya Patel (Customer Success Manager) — priya@redwood.ai
- Technical liaison: Jonas Rivera (Solutions Eng) — jrivera@redwood.ai
- Emergency escalation: support@redwood.ai (24/7)

Draft status and review notes:
- This is a working draft for customer-facing recon and replay choices. Please review for tone and legal phrasing with Legal if you plan to attach the acknowledgement template.
- Internal owners: CS lead (Priya), Solutions Eng (Jonas), Applied ML lead (Maya) — expected internal sign-off by 2026-08-28.

Attachments/links (for customers):
- Evidence bundle link (will be generated per-tenant after you opt-in)
- Replay sandbox instructions: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/REPLAY/Replay-Sandbox-Guide
- Incident technical log (internal): https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/INF-4521

End of draft.
